BiblicalUsage: The word is harlotry, and in the prophets it means idolatry. Jerusalem trusted in her beauty and played the harlot, multiplying her whoredoms at every head of the way; Oholibah saw her sister's ways and was more corrupt in her inordinate love; and God says, Because thou hast forgotten Me, and cast Me behind thy back, therefore bear thou also thy lewdness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe harlotry in the prophets is never only about the body: it is a people giving to idols the love that belongs to God. My position is that idolatry is adultery, and the God who names it is the husband who was betrayed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
